facts: $y=\arcsin x$ is the reflection of $y=\sin x$, restricted to $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}$, in the line $y=x$.
$y=\arcsin x$ has domain $-1\le x\le1$ and range $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le y\le\frac{\pi}{2}$, increasing from $\left(-1,-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ to $\left(1,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
$y=\arccos x$ is the reflection of $y=\cos x$, restricted to $0\le x\le\pi$, in the line $y=x$.
$y=\arccos x$ has domain $-1\le x\le1$ and range $0\le y\le\pi$, decreasing from $(-1,\pi)$ to $(1,0)$.
$y=\arctan x$ is the reflection of $y=\tan x$, restricted to $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$, in the line $y=x$.
$y=\arctan x$ has domain all real $x$ and range $-\frac{\pi}{2}<y<\frac{\pi}{2}$.
The vertical asymptotes $x=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$ of the restricted $y=\tan x$ become the horizontal asymptotes $y=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$ of $y=\arctan x$.
$y=\arcsin x$ and $y=\arccos x$ stop at endpoints where $x=\pm1$, so neither of them has an asymptote.
steps: Sketch the restricted trigonometric graph over its principal domain.
Reflect the restricted graph in the line $y=x$ by swapping the coordinates of the key points.
Swap the domain and the range, turning any vertical asymptote into a horizontal asymptote.
Sketch the inverse curve through the reflected key points and state its domain and range.

workedExamples.question_text: Sketch $y=\arcsin x$ by reflecting the principal restricted sine graph in $y=x$. State its domain, range, asymptotes, parity and whether it is increasing or decreasing. Mark the point corresponding to $\left(-\frac{\pi}{6},-\frac12\right)$ on the restricted sine graph.

Sketch $y=\arccos x$ by reflecting the principal restricted cosine graph in $y=x$. State its domain, range, asymptotes, parity and whether it is increasing or decreasing. Mark the point corresponding to $\left(\frac{2\pi}{3},-\frac12\right)$ on the restricted cosine graph.
Sketch $y=\arctan x$ by reflecting $y=\tan x$ for $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$ in $y=x$. Show its asymptotes, state its domain and range, and mark the point where $x=-1$.
On the interval $-\frac12\le x\le\frac12$, sketch $y=\arcsin x$ and $y=\arccos x$ on the same axes. By adding ordinates, sketch $y=\arcsin x+\arccos x$ on that interval, including its endpoints.

foundation.solution_text:
Reflecting in $y=x$ swaps the domain and the range of the restricted graph.
Restricted $y=\sin x$ has domain $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}$ and range $-1\le y\le1$.
Domain of $y=\arcsin x$: $-1\le x\le1$
Range of $y=\arcsin x$: $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le y\le\frac{\pi}{2}$

Reflecting in $y=x$ swaps the domain and the range of the restricted graph.
Restricted $y=\cos x$ has domain $0\le x\le\pi$ and range $-1\le y\le1$.
Domain of $y=\arccos x$: $-1\le x\le1$
Range of $y=\arccos x$: $0\le y\le\pi$

foundation.question_text: State whether the graph of $y=\arcsin x$ is increasing or decreasing, and whether the function is odd, even or neither.
foundation.solution_text:
The graph increases from $\left(-1,-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ to $\left(1,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, so it is increasing.
It is symmetric about the origin, so $y=\arcsin x$ is odd.

foundation.question_text: State whether the graph of $y=\arccos x$ is increasing or decreasing, and whether the function is odd, even or neither.
foundation.solution_text:
The graph decreases from $(-1,\pi)$ to $(1,0)$, so it is decreasing.
It is symmetric about neither the origin nor the $y$-axis, so $y=\arccos x$ is neither odd nor even.

Reflecting in $y=x$ turns a vertical asymptote $x=k$ into a horizontal asymptote $y=k$.
$x=\frac{\pi}{2}\to y=\frac{\pi}{2}$
$x=-\frac{\pi}{2}\to y=-\frac{\pi}{2}$

foundation.question_text: State the domain and range of $y=\arctan x$.
foundation.solution_text:
The restricted $y=\tan x$ has domain $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$ and range all real numbers.
Reflecting in $y=x$ swaps the domain and range.
Domain of $y=\arctan x$: all real $x$
Range of $y=\arctan x$: $-\frac{\pi}{2}<y<\frac{\pi}{2}$

development.question_text: Sketch $y=\arccos x$ and state whether it has any asymptotes.

development.solution_text:
Both restricted graphs have range $-1\le y\le1$, and reflecting in $y=x$ makes that the domain.
Common domain: $-1\le x\le1$
Range of $y=\arcsin x$: $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le y\le\frac{\pi}{2}$
Range of $y=\arccos x$: $0\le y\le\pi$
